brief_scope: Portable local-workspace backup and preview-first restore for structured records, attachments, and preferences; interruption/removable storage; inventory and damage; empty restore and deliberate merge; identity/references; newer schemas and migrations; atomicity; passphrase option, metadata, diagnostics, no invented recovery; whole versus incremental; validation plan.

review_method.released_plan_hash_check: SHA-256 of discovery.md and revealed-plan.md matched the values in plan-reveal.json.
review_method.execution_status: Documentation review and static plan-hash comparison only. No archive/storage/application/migration/crypto/fault-injection/user-data checks were run.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API and sqlite3_backup C interface
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite C interface documentation; unversioned, consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Online Backup API overview and sqlite3_backup_step/finish, lines 34-79; alternatives at lines 81-85.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official API documentation and checked snapshot behavior, read-lock duration, retryable BUSY/LOCKED, fatal IOERR/NOMEM/READONLY, rollback on incomplete completion, and destination-handle restrictions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Source reads are locked per step, not continuously. External writes may cause the operation to restart; writes through the same source connection are reflected in the backup. BUSY/LOCKED can be retried; IOERR/NOMEM/READONLY are fatal. The destination connection must not be used between init and finish.
sources.applicability: Only if SQLite is selected. Gives a database-level copy, not a cross-resource snapshot of separate attachments or preferences.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging documentation and WAL-reset bug notice
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite documentation; unversioned. Notice states likely affected 3.7.0 through 3.51.2; fixed 3.51.3+ and backports 3.44.6/3.50.7.
sources.locator: WAL persistence and commit/checkpoint sections around lines 82-96; WAL-reset bug lines 191-197.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official WAL page and checked committed-WAL persistence, sidecar separation, exact version range and concurrency trigger.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A WAL commit can be recorded in -wal without yet being copied into the main database; separating a live database from WAL state is unsafe. The announced corruption bug requires WAL mode, at least two connections to the same file in separate threads/processes, and concurrent write/checkpoint activity. It is described as a narrow race.
sources.applicability: Conditional on the product using SQLite WAL and on the bundled engine release/concurrency pattern. It is not evidence that backup alone triggers the bug.

sources.title: SQLite PRAGMA reference
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite reference; unversioned, consulted 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: foreign_key_check lines 366 onward; foreign_keys lines 379-390; integrity_check lines 492-513; user_version lines 933-941.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official reference and checked user_version semantics, integrity-check coverage, foreign-key-check separation, and foreign-key enforcement defaults/overrides.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: user_version is an integer applications may use; SQLite itself does not interpret it. integrity_check does not find FK errors. foreign_keys historically defaulted OFF from 3.6.19, can be compile-time overridden, and may change in a future release; applications should set the required behavior.
sources.applicability: Only if SQLite is selected. Engine-level checks do not prove attachment existence or application-level validity.

sources.title: Python 3.15 zipfile library documentation
sources.locator: ZipFile.testzip() lines 231-235; Path objects and sanitization note lines 288-298; ZIP64 notes around lines 383-391.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Python documentation and checked CRC/header test scope and untrusted-name validation responsibility for zipfile.Path.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: testzip reads members and checks CRCs and headers, returning the first bad filename or None. zipfile.Path itself does not sanitize archive names; callers must validate. These are Python API details.
sources.applicability: Implementation-specific evidence for Python ZIP tooling; the general need for exact inventory and safe extraction does not require Python.

sources.title: GHSA-94vh-gphv-8pm8 — Rust zip archive extraction path canonicalization flaw
sources.released_version_or_commit: Published 2025-03-16; affected zip crate versions >=1.3.0; patched version 2.3.0.
sources.locator: Advisory summary and details, lines 131-157: earlier symlink followed by later extraction through it.
sources.observed_operation: Read the public advisory and checked affected/patched versions and extraction sequence.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A malicious archive can place a symlink to a parent directory before a later file; the affected extraction routine failed to validate the final canonicalized path.
sources.applicability: Directly relevant if this crate and affected versions are used. Otherwise supports an explicit symlink-order regression case, not a claim about every extractor.

sources.title: age file encryption format v1.0.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: Pinned age format specification v1.0.0. The page states this is an older edition and points to v1.1.0.
sources.locator: Header/version/MAC lines 15-54; payload chunking/final chunk lines 82-95; scrypt stanza rules lines 157-181.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the pinned specification and checked its header, AEAD payload, scrypt wrapping, final-chunk, and recipient-stanza conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Passphrase wrapping uses scrypt and ChaCha20-Poly1305. Payload uses authenticated 64 KiB chunks and streaming decryption must fail without a valid final chunk. An scrypt stanza must be the sole header stanza.
sources.applicability: Candidate format only; no library/package is selected. Describes encryption/integrity behavior, not archive semantics, source validity, author identity, or service recovery.

sources.title: restic 0.19.1 backup documentation
sources.locator: Snapshot/deduplication model lines 65-118; incomplete source-read exit status and explanation lines 448-460.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official restic documentation and checked deduplication, snapshot model, and incomplete source-read behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If some source files cannot be read, restic can still create an incomplete snapshot and returns status 3; status 0 means snapshot with all source files, while fatal errors return 1 with no snapshot.
sources.applicability: Alternative repository model only. It does not provide this application's logical cross-store snapshot, domain-aware preview, or migrations.

sources.title: Rust std::fs::rename documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling stable Rust standard-library documentation; API stable since Rust 1.0.0.
sources.locator: Function semantics and platform-specific behavior lines 21-45.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Rust docs and checked replacement behavior, same-filesystem requirement, and Unix/Windows directory cases.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Cross-mount rename fails. Existing-target directory replacement differs by platform/filesystem. The docs do not establish power-loss durability.
sources.applicability: Conditional on using Rust std::fs and on target OS/filesystem; does not prove an atomic multi-file workspace transaction.

sources.title: NIST FIPS 180-4 Update 1, Secure Hash Standard
sources.released_version_or_commit: Final FIPS 180-4 Update 1, published 2015-08-04; page notes a later planned revision.
sources.locator: Publication abstract and history; hash algorithms and message digest purpose.
sources.observed_operation: Opened NIST publication page and checked its statement of digest purpose.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The standard specifies hash digests used to detect changes since digest generation. A digest alone does not bind an independently replaceable digest to an author or trusted source.
sources.applicability: Supports manifest digests for change detection when the manifest is trusted/authenticated; does not replace authenticated encryption or a separately designed signature/trust channel.

sources.title: age file encryption format v1.1.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: age format specification v1.1.0, the latest edition identified by the v1.0.0 page at access time.
sources.locator: Encrypted file/header lines 14-54; payload authentication lines 81-93; scrypt stanza and sole-stanza rule lines 192-216; tagged recipient additions after line 217.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the current edition and independently checked the passphrase, payload, final-chunk, header, and recipient rules against v1.0.0.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Scrypt remains the passphrase mechanism and remains the only header stanza if used. The 64 KiB authenticated payload chunks and final-chunk requirement remain. v1.1 adds tagged recipient types, but they cannot be mixed with an scrypt stanza.
sources.applicability: Use for current-version qualification if age is considered; still no selected library, package, or recovery design. Encryption does not prove archive authorship or source validity.

sources.title: SQLite VACUUM and VACUUM INTO
sources.released_version_or_commit: Live official SQLite documentation, page last updated 2025-07-12.
sources.locator: VACUUM INTO semantics and interruption/durability conditions, lines 40-48.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and checked snapshot consistency, destination precondition, interrupted output, and synchronous-mode flush caveat.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: VACUUM INTO is a consistent snapshot; unplanned shutdown/power loss during the operation may leave incomplete/corrupt output. The stated post-completion protection depends on NORMAL/FULL synchronous plus functioning OS/filesystem/hardware.
sources.applicability: Only if SQLite VACUUM INTO is selected. Keep output private until the command completes and independent verification passes.
